case.question: I fish for salmon from a boat. For this week, how good do you expect boat fishing for salmon to be at each of St. Joseph, South Haven, Grand Haven and Muskegon? Rate each port 0-4 (0 slow, 1 below average, 2 average, 3 good, 4 excellent) and say which you'd go to.

events.text:
## Recommendation
- **Go to Muskegon by boat.** My expected rating is **3 (good)**.
- **Grand Haven is the next choice**, expected **2 (average)**. South Haven and St. Joseph are expected to be **2** and **1–2**. I'd expect St. Joseph to be the weakest.
- **Fish 80 feet of water or deeper, out from the pierheads.** Run glow plugs or glow spoons, and green meat rigs or flasher-fly rigs if you're near the bottom of the range.
- Start in about 80–110 feet and move out to 180–230 feet if the fish aren't there. Expected ratings are my inference from the last few weeks of reports, not a forecast.

## Why
- Muskegon's newest boat report was the best of the four: the Aug 27 report rated boats good (3) in water out to 80 feet, with glow plugs and glow spoons working well (Muskegon, 2025-08-27).
- Grand Haven's boat fishing has been average to good for three weeks, with 3 on Aug 20 and 2 on Aug 27, so it's the reliable second choice (Grand Haven, 2025-08-20; Grand Haven, 2025-08-27).
- St. Joseph and South Haven have been slow more often than not, with boat ratings of 0 on Aug 13 and Aug 20 (St. Joseph, 2025-08-20; South Haven, 2025-08-13).
- I'd expect the bite to be deeper and more scattered than in early August. The fish were 50–100 feet down in the latest good reports, and the water has warmed (Grand Haven, 2025-08-20).

## Evidence
**Recent reports** (newest is Aug 27, six days before today)
- **Muskegon, Aug 27:** boat quality 3. "Anglers caught salmon from inside the basin out to 80 feet of water… Glow plugs and glow spoons worked well." Water up to 80 ft.
- **Grand Haven, Aug 27:** boat quality 2. "Boat anglers caught decent numbers of salmon from the pierheads out to 80 feet of water." Glow spoons and glow plugs were best.
- **South Haven, Aug 27:** boat quality 2. Fish came from 35 feet "out to well past 120 feet," mostly on spoons. The report called conditions challenging.
- **St. Joseph, Aug 27:** boat quality 2. "Most boats targeting around 70 feet of water… Most fish were caught on spoons." Fish were "very spread out."
- **Grand Haven, Aug 20:** boat quality 3. Best fish were "50 to 100 feet down in 80 to 220 feet of water," on glow spoons, glow plugs and flasher flies.
- **Muskegon, Aug 20:** boat quality 2. Most fish were "50 to 100 feet down" on plugs and green flasher-fly rigs.
- **South Haven, Aug 20:** boat quality 0. "Salmon fishing was slow… very scattered."
- **St. Joseph, Aug 20:** boat quality 0. "Boats had been fishing mostly beyond 100 feet of water."
- **Piers:** slow to poor at Grand Haven and Muskegon through August, so I'd stay off the piers for now (Grand Haven, 2025-08-20; Muskegon, 2025-08-13).

**Past seasons:** I didn't pull historical matches for this question, so I have no historical comparison here.

**Conditions now** (from the tool's backtest summary, not live data)
- St. Joseph buoy: 72 F, flat over the week.
- South Haven buoy: 70 F, flat over the week.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon buoy: 65 F, up 9 F over the week.
- Live modeled cold-layer depth and wind forecast were not available, so I can't say where the 55 F water is or whether wind will be a problem.

## Caveats
- **Report age:** the newest report is from Aug 27, six days ago. Fall conditions can change within a week.
- **Current water:** the buoy readings are summarized from the week before today, not live. The 9 F rise at Grand Haven and Muskegon is a warming trend, not an upwelling sign.
- **No wind forecast:** check the wind before you go. For a small boat, strong wind or big waves should send you to the pier or the river instead.
- **Ratings are estimates:** the expected 0–4 ratings are my inference from the last 3–4 weeks of reports.

## Sources
- Michigan DNR, Aug 27 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3efbfed
- Michigan DNR, Aug 20 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3eeac7b
- Michigan DNR, Aug 13 bulletin: https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/3edac95
